'''United Infrastructure''' (formerly '''United Living Group''') is a construction company.<ref name="unitedliving.co.uk">{{cite web|url=http://www.unitedliving.co.uk/|title=Home - United Living|publisher=|accessdate=28 March 2016}}</ref> In 2023, [[Apollo Global Management]] completed the purchase of the company.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.elysiancapital.com/news/all-news/elysian-capital-completes-sale-of-united-living-group,-a-leading-provider-of-essential-infrastructure,-social-housing-and-construction-services-across-the-uk/|title=Elysian Capital completes sale of United Living Group, a leading provider of Essential Infrastructure, Social Housing and Construction Services across the UK|work=Elysian Capital|access-date=2023-12-15|language=en}}</ref>

==History==
The company was formed from the merger of Bullock Construction Ltd and [[United House|United House Ltd]] (the contracting division of United House Group)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.unitedliving.co.uk/directions|title=Projects - United Living|publisher=|accessdate=28 March 2016}}</ref> in September 2014 <ref name="ldc.co.uk">{{cite web|url=http://www.ldc.co.uk/portfolio/companyinfo.aspx?Id=305|title=Our Portfolio|author=LDC|date=18 February 2016|work=ldc.co.uk|accessdate=28 March 2016}}</ref> [[Lloyds Development Capital]] (LDC) had an ownership stake in both companies: in April 2008 LDC invested in the management buy-out of Bullock Construction Limited <ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ldc.co.uk/portfolio/companyinfo.aspx?Id=273|title=Our Portfolio|author=LDC|date=18 February 2016|work=ldc.co.uk|accessdate=28 March 2016}}</ref> and in March 2010, United House secured financial backing from LDC to continue its expansion.<ref name="ldc.co.uk"/>

===United House===
The origin of United House lies with Geoffrey Granter who founded it as Harp Heating in 1964. Initially, the core business was installing [[central heating]] in [[council housing]] while the tenants remained in occupation. 
Harp Heating broadened this service into an internal refurbishment product for the [[Greater London Council|GLC]].
Michael Rayfield was joint MD with Geoffrey Granter of Harp heating before the group changed its name.
After Jeffrey Adams joined the company in 1981, becoming its joint owner with Granter, the company changed its name to United House and expanded into housebuilding and housing refurbishment. In the 1990s, the company won business under the [[Private Finance Initiative]] linked to the [[Decent Homes Programme]].<ref name=Harrington>{{cite news|last=Harrington|first=Ben|title=Builders set for fortune in United House disposal|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/finance/newsbysector/constructionandproperty/2790906/Builders-set-for-fortune-in-United-House-disposal.html|accessdate=12 October 2011|newspaper=Daily Telegraph|date=1 June 2008}}</ref>
A development division named Modern City Living was established in 1990.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.unitedhousedevelopments.net/about-us/our-history|title=Our History|publisher=|accessdate=28 March 2016}}</ref> 
In 2008, Modern City Living was rebranded United House Developments.

Granter retired from the business in 2008 and Steven Halbert joined the board as chairman. [[Lloyds Development Capital]] (LDC) invested a minority stake and [[Royal Bank of Scotland|RBS]] provided bank loans to fund further expansion in [[inner city]] private housebuilding.<ref>{{cite news|last=Stothart|first=Chloë|title=Lloyds buys stake in United House|url=http://www.insidehousing.co.uk/news/finance/lloyds-buys-stake-in-united-house/6509487.article|accessdate=12 October 2011|newspaper=Inside Housing|date=21 April 2010}}</ref>

===Merged company===
On 16 September 2014, a restructuring of United House Group was announced. United House's construction business (United House Ltd) merged with Bullock Construction, which was also owned by LDC. The new construction company was called United Living Group,<ref name="unitedliving.co.uk"/> and Bullock's CEO Ian Burnett become the Group Chief Executive. Later in 2014, [[United House Developments]], headed by Adams as chairman and Rick de Blaby as CEO, became a separate [[property development|development]] company, based in London.<ref>{{cite news|first=Robyn |last=Wilson |url=https://www.constructionnews.co.uk/buildings/sectors/united-house-and-bullock-construction-merger-to-create-300m-turnover-firm-16-09-2014/ |title=United House and Bullock Construction to merge |newspaper=Construction News |date=16 September 2014|accessdate=16 September 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|first=Grant |last=Prior |url=http://www.constructionenquirer.com/2014/09/16/bullock-to-merge-with-united-house/|title=Loss-making United House to merge with Bullock |newspaper=Construction Enquirer |date=16 September 2014|accessdate=17 September 2014}}</ref>

The new brand United Living Group was launched on 1 April 2015.

=== Acquisition by Fastflow Group ===
In 2019, United Living was acquired by Fastflow Group bringing together their construction, utilities and property maintenance businesses. Fastflow Group CEO, Neil Armstrong becoming CEO and chairman of the new group. In January 2023, the business reported pre-tax losses of around £21m for the second year running, on revenue of £437m.<ref name="Morby-09Jan2023">{{cite news |last1=Morby |first1=Aaron |title=United Living Holdings records £21m pre-tax loss |url=https://www.constructionenquirer.com/2023/01/09/united-living-holdings-records-21m-pre-tax-loss/ |access-date=9 January 2023 |work=Construction Enquirer |date=9 January 2023}}</ref>

=== Acquisition of Wood’s UK Transmission & Distribution business ===
In December 2025, it was announced United Infrastructure had agreed to acquire [[John Wood Group]]’s UK Transmission & Distribution business for £57.5 million. The purchase would add engineering and installation capabilities in overhead line and underground cable projects to the company’s existing infrastructure portfolio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Media |first=Insider |date=2025-12-11 |title=United Infrastructure agrees £57.5m acquisition of Wood’s UK T&D business - Insider Media |url=https://www.insidermedia.com/news/national/united-infrastructure-agrees-57.5m-acquisition-of-woods-uk-td-business |access-date=2025-12-11 |website=Insider Media Ltd |language=en}}</ref>
